subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is a personal factor that can affect a person's participation in physical activity?
options: The colour of the team kit
The brand of the match ball
questions.explain: Age is one of the recognised factors (alongside gender, ethnicity, disability and socio-economic group) that influences participation.

questions.q: Which of the following is generally considered an under-represented group in sport?
questions.explain: People with disabilities, women, older adults and some ethnic groups are commonly under-represented in sport participation.

questions.q: Why might a lack of role models reduce participation among a particular group?
options: There are fewer successful people to aspire to and identify with in that sport
It makes match tickets more expensive
It increases the number of qualified coaches
It improves television coverage of the sport
questions.explain: Without visible role models to identify with, people may feel the sport is not for them, lowering participation.

questions.q: A sports centre introduces women-only swimming sessions. This is best described as a strategy to:
options: Increase participation among an under-represented group
Reduce the number of available coaches
questions.explain: Targeted sessions remove barriers for specific groups and are a common strategy to raise participation.

questions.q: A local council wants to increase participation among older adults. Which initiative is most appropriate?
options: A high-intensity competitive league open only to under-18s
questions.explain: Low-impact, affordable, accessible activities at convenient times directly target older adults' barriers to participation.

questions.q: Which factor, linked to a person's income and background, can affect their participation in sport?
questions.explain: Socio-economic group affects the cost, time and access available for sport, influencing participation.

questions.q: The 'golden triangle' describes the interrelationship between sport and which two other elements?
questions.explain: The golden triangle shows the interdependence of sport, the media and sponsorship/business, each benefiting the others.

questions.q: Which of the following is a type of sponsorship a performer might receive?
questions.explain: Sponsorship can be financial, or take the form of free kit, equipment or facilities.

questions.q: Which of the following is a positive effect of commercialisation on a performer?
options: They can earn more money and train full-time
They are no longer allowed on television
They receive less funding for training
questions.explain: Commercial income lets performers train full-time and improve, a key positive effect of commercialisation.

questions.q: Which of the following is a negative effect of media coverage on live sport?
options: Kick-off times may be changed to suit TV audiences, inconveniencing live spectators
Stadiums are made larger for fans
There is less money available in the sport
questions.explain: Media influence can alter scheduling to suit broadcasts, which can disadvantage spectators attending in person.

questions.q: A sportswear company pays a tennis player to wear its clothing during matches. What is the company's main aim?
options: To increase brand awareness and sell more products
To have the player banned from the sport
questions.explain: Sponsors invest to raise brand awareness and boost sales, gaining exposure through the performer.

questions.q: A broadcaster pays a large fee for exclusive rights to show a league. A likely negative effect for fans is that:
options: They may have to pay a subscription to watch their team
All matches become free to watch
Every stadium is forced to close
questions.explain: Exclusive paid rights can put coverage behind subscriptions, so fans pay more to watch their team.

questions.q: Which of the following is a form of media used to cover sport?
questions.explain: Media forms include television, the internet, social media and newspapers.

questions.q: Sportsmanship is best defined as:
options: Playing fairly, within the rules and the spirit of the game
Bending the rules to gain an unfair advantage
questions.explain: Sportsmanship means competing fairly and with respect, upholding both the rules and the spirit of the game.

questions.q: Gamesmanship refers to:
options: Using tactics that stretch the rules without breaking them to gain an advantage
Always competing with complete fair play
questions.explain: Gamesmanship bends the spirit of the rules for advantage without technically breaking them.

questions.q: Shaking an opponent's hand and congratulating them after losing a match is an example of:
questions.explain: Showing respect and fair play towards an opponent, even in defeat, is sportsmanship.

questions.q: Deliberately wasting time near the end of a match to protect a narrow lead is an example of:
questions.explain: Time-wasting stretches the rules to gain an advantage without breaking them, which is gamesmanship.

questions.q: Why might an endurance athlete illegally use EPO (erythropoietin)?
options: To increase red blood cell count and oxygen delivery to the muscles
To calm their nerves before shooting
To lose weight rapidly before a weigh-in
questions.explain: EPO raises red blood cell count, increasing oxygen delivery and aerobic endurance, which is why it is banned.

questions.q: An archer wants to steady their hands and reduce anxiety before shooting. Which banned drug type would illegally produce this effect?
questions.explain: Beta blockers reduce heart rate and anxiety, steadying the hands, giving an unfair advantage in precision sports.

questions.q: A sprinter tests positive for anabolic steroids. A likely consequence for the athlete is:
options: A ban from competition and damage to their reputation
questions.explain: Doping leads to sanctions such as bans and loss of reputation, sponsorship and records.
